skill.name: controlnet-pose
skill.description: Generate pose-conditioned images and motion-controlled videos through RunComfy. The skill selects Kling, Wan, or Z-Image routes from the requested media and control type.
skill.summary: Route pose and motion references to suitable RunComfy generation models.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer mostly mistook Markdown syntax, documentation links, and placeholder URLs for executable behavior. Two contextual risks remain: unpinned package execution and shell examples that can become injectable when an agent substitutes unescaped user input.

remediation.issue: The installation examples execute an unpinned npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin an audited CLI version and integrity reference. Avoid automatic npx installation in agent-run instructions.

remediation.issue: User-controlled values are shown inside single-quoted shell JSON.
remediation.suggestion: Build arguments with a structured process API or a temporary JSON file. Do not interpolate user content into shell command text.

remediation.issue: The text claims there is no shell-injection surface.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the absolute claim and document required escaping for apostrophes, newlines, and shell metacharacters.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Quoting for User-Controlled Inputs
semantic_findings.description: Examples place JSON inside single-quoted shell arguments while prompts and URLs can come from users. An apostrophe can end the quote and enable command injection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples visibly use single-quoted JSON, and the skill expects an agent to insert user prompts or URLs. Runtime escaping behavior is not specified.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Installation and Execution
semantic_findings.description: The installation guidance runs the latest @runcomfy/cli package, including automatic npx installation. Version drift or package compromise would execute new code with user privileges.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both installation examples omit a version, and npx uses the automatic approval flag. This creates a clear dependency supply-chain exposure.

content.value_statement: Pose and motion references are difficult to route across image and video generation models. This skill selects a suitable RunComfy model and prepares the generation request.
actual_capabilities: Classifies requests as video motion transfer or still-image pose conditioning.
Selects Kling Motion Control Pro or Standard for reference-video motion transfer.
Selects Wan 2-2 Animate for stylized character animation.
Selects Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA for pose, depth, or canny image control.
Prepares RunComfy CLI requests with model inputs and output directories.
Directs complex multi-condition requests to hosted ComfyUI workflows.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, an authenticated account, and network access.
Reference videos, character images, and control images must be available through usable URLs.
Direct CLI routes support single-condition workflows, not complex ControlNet stacks.
Generation quality depends on reference framing, model behavior, and third-party service availability.

use_cases.title: Transfer Performance Motion
use_cases.description: Apply a reference performance video to a target character with Kling Motion Control.

use_cases.title: Lock an Image Pose
use_cases.description: Generate a new image from an OpenPose, DWPose, depth, or canny control image.

use_cases.title: Prototype Character Animation
use_cases.description: Route stylized animation drafts to Wan or lower-cost Kling models before final rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Pose-Controlled Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an image of [subject] in [setting] using this [OpenPose or DWPose] control image: [URL]. Save the result in [folder].

prompt_templates.title: Transfer Motion to a Character
prompt_templates.prompt: Transfer the motion from [reference video URL] to [character image URL]. Use [Pro or Standard] quality and save the generated video in [folder].

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Model for a Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare suitable RunComfy routes for [project]. The input is [media type], the style is [style], and the control reference is [type and URL].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Condition Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a workflow using [pose], [depth], and [reference image] controls for [goal]. Identify whether CLI routes suffice or a ComfyUI workflow is required.

output_examples.input: Use this dance video to animate my illustrated character.
output_examples.output: Selected Kling Motion Control Pro for video motion transfer. Requested the reference video and character image URLs before generation.

output_examples.input: Create a samurai image in this OpenPose stance.
output_examples.output: Selected Z-Image Turbo ControlNet LoRA for still-image pose conditioning. Prepared the control image, prompt, and output location.

output_examples.input: Use pose and depth controls together for a product scene.
output_examples.output: Identified a multi-condition request and recommended a hosted ComfyUI workflow instead of a single-condition CLI endpoint.

best_practices: Use clean, well-framed references with one clear subject and continuous motion.
Confirm the control type matches the selected model or LoRA.
Review service privacy requirements before sending prompts or media URLs.
anti_patterns: Do not use still-image routes for video motion transfer.
Do not send multi-condition stacks to a single-condition CLI endpoint.
Do not interpolate untrusted text directly into a shell command.

faq.question: What inputs does video motion transfer require?
faq.answer: It requires a reference performance video URL and a target character image URL.

faq.question: Which controls work for still images?
faq.answer: The documented route supports pose skeletons, DWPose, canny edges, and depth maps when the selected LoRA matches.

faq.question: Can it combine pose, depth, and reference controls?
faq.answer: Not through the documented direct endpoint. Use a dedicated hosted ComfyUI workflow for multi-condition stacks.

faq.question: Does it generate control images?
faq.answer: No. Create pose skeletons or other control images with a separate preprocessor before using this skill.

faq.question: Where are generated files stored?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads results to the output directory selected for the request.

faq.question: Does it require authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. Sign in with the RunComfy CLI or provide the documented token environment variable in automated environments.
